statement: The evolving memory-control layer consists of experiential memory, a working-memory specification, an invocation policy, and checker set.
Working state records each goal's content, status, supporting evidence, and optional blocker.
A fixed kernel commits only state transitions supported by explicit checker results over environment evidence.
Skill invocation is grounded in verified working state and a defined execution event rather than selected from the full history.
Failure-driven patches are scoped to diagnosed memory components and non-implicated components are copied unchanged.
Candidate patches are admitted only after repairing the source task and satisfying a held-out anchor regression criterion.
The reference engine uses deterministic Python callbacks for checkers and evaluators.
Recuris improves task success in 35 of 37 completed model-benchmark pairs.
evidence: reported by paper; no local benchmark reproduction

statement: On Terminal-Bench 2.1, most headline improvement is explained by retry budget; matched-budget adaptation adds 2.3 points with p=0.774.
evidence: reported by paper; retained as an anti-overclaim constraint
